resources.title: Attached
resources.author: Amir Levine & Rachel Heller
resources.description: The definitive guide to adult attachment theory. Explains anxious, avoidant, and secure styles in plain language and why we are drawn to people who feel familiar, not safe.

resources.title: Trauma Rewired
resources.author: Jennifer Wallace & Elisabeth Kristof
resources.description: A research-backed podcast on how trauma lives in the body and how the nervous system can heal. Particularly useful for understanding why no-contact feels physically painful.

resources.title: Psykologiguiden
resources.description: Swedish directory for finding a licensed therapist. Searchable by location, specialisation, and insurance. If you are ready to talk to someone, this is a good place to start. (Swedish)

resources.title: The Body Keeps the Score
resources.author: Bessel van der Kolk
resources.description: A landmark book on how trauma shapes the body and mind — and the range of approaches that can help. Particularly relevant if the relationship involved emotional or psychological abuse.

resources.title: We Can Do Hard Things
resources.author: Glennon Doyle
resources.description: Honest, warm conversations about difficult human experiences. Not specifically about breakups, but consistently useful for anyone going through something hard.

resources.title: Psychology Today Therapist Finder
resources.description: International directory of licensed therapists, searchable by issue, therapy type, and location. A practical starting point if you are considering professional support.

resources.title: Why Does He Do That?
resources.author: Lundy Bancroft
resources.description: A clear-eyed look at controlling and abusive relationship dynamics — written for people who are still trying to understand what happened. Widely recommended by therapists.

resources.title: Getting Past Your Breakup
resources.author: Susan J. Elliott
resources.description: A practical, structured guide to breakup recovery grounded in cognitive-behavioural principles. More hands-on than most self-help books on the topic — exercises included.

resources.title: Relationship Alive
resources.author: Neil Sattin
resources.description: In-depth interviews with leading researchers and therapists on attachment, intimacy, and relationships. Useful for understanding what went wrong and what healthy looks like.

resources.title: BACP Find a Therapist
resources.description: The British Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy's therapist directory. Searchable by location and speciality. Accredited practitioners only. (UK)

resources.title: Running on Empty
resources.author: Jonice Webb
resources.description: On childhood emotional neglect — the invisible wound that often shapes who we are drawn to in relationships. Quietly illuminating for many people in or after difficult relationships.

resources.title: The Holistic Psychologist
resources.author: Dr Nicole LePera
resources.description: Accessible content on self-healing, nervous system regulation, and breaking relational patterns. Instagram and website both useful; start with the self-healing protocol.

resources.title: How to Heal a Broken Heart
resources.author: Huberman Lab
resources.description: Andrew Huberman and Dr. Paul Conti cover the neuroscience of heartbreak, grief, and loss — why it feels so physical, and what the brain and body need to recover.

resources.title: The Wisdom of Trauma
resources.author: Trauma Rewired
resources.description: Elisabeth Kristof on how unresolved relational trauma lives in the body — and the difference between numbing it and actually healing it. One of the most-shared episodes of the show.

resources.title: Who Are You Without Them?
resources.author: We Can Do Hard Things
resources.description: Glennon Doyle and Abby Wambach on how relationships change who we think we are — and how to find yourself again when one ends. Warm and direct.
